level1.text: The end of a long coil spring is shaken sideways, and a transverse wave with a frequency of $4.0\,\text{Hz}$ and a wavelength of $0.75\,\text{m}$ travels in the spring. What is the speed of the wave?
A loudspeaker plays a note whose frequency is $440\,\text{Hz}$. The sound travels in the air of the room at a speed of $343\,\text{m/s}$. How long is the wavelength of the sound?
In a taut rope a wave travels at a speed of $6.0\,\text{m/s}$, and the distance between the crests of the wave is $1.5\,\text{m}$. At what frequency is the end of the rope shaken?
The wave machine of an indoor wave pool makes waves whose period is $2.5\,\text{s}$ and wavelength $4.0\,\text{m}$. At what speed do the waves travel?
In a rope a wave travels at a speed of $4.8\,\text{m/s}$, and its wavelength is $1.2\,\text{m}$. What is the period of the wave?

level2.text: The graph shows the displacement of one point of a taut rope as a function of time when the end of the rope is shaken steadily. From a snapshot of the rope it has been measured that the distance between successive crests is $1.0\,\text{m}$. Read the necessary value from the graph. What is the speed of the wave?

A student shakes the end of a long skipping rope steadily and counts that the hand makes $18$ full swings in $12.0$ seconds. The distance between the crests of the rope is $1.40\,\text{m}$. What is the speed of the wave in the rope?

The sound of a loudspeaker at the edge of a pool travels in air at a speed of $343\,\text{m/s}$, and its wavelength in air is $0.750\,\text{m}$. The sound continues into water, where it travels at a speed of $1480\,\text{m/s}$. How long is the wavelength of the sound in water?

The longitudinal wave of an earthquake travels in the bedrock. A seismometer measures the frequency of the wave as $0.50\,\text{Hz}$, and the wavelength is $12\,\text{km}$. What is the speed of the wave in metres per second?

level3.text: Two photographs are taken of a rope at an interval of $0.15\,\text{s}$. In the first picture a crest is at $x = 0.60\,\text{m}$ and in the second at $x = 1.05\,\text{m}$, and between the pictures the crest has not had time to travel one wavelength. In both pictures the distance between successive crests is $1.20\,\text{m}$. At what frequency is the end of the rope shaken? Also justify why the displacement of the crest is not a displacement of the matter of the rope.

One end of a long railway rail is struck with a hammer. A listener at the other end of the rail hears two bangs: first the sound that came along the rail and $0.50\,\text{s}$ later the sound that came through the air. Sound travels in steel at a speed of $5100\,\text{m/s}$ and in air at $340\,\text{m/s}$. How long is the rail? Justify why the same blow of the hammer produces two sounds that arrive at different times.

A wave goes round a stadium stand: every spectator stands up $0.050\,\text{s}$ later than the one sitting next to them and then sits down again. The distance between adjacent seats is $0.55\,\text{m}$, and the length of the row going round the stand is $440\,\text{m}$. How long does it take for the wave to go once round the stand? Justify why the wave travels although no spectator changes places.
